papers.title: Detecting and Preventing Data Poisoning Attacks on AI Models
papers.abstract: This paper investigates the critical issue of data poisoning attacks on AI models, a growing concern in the ever-evolving landscape of artificial intelligence and cybersecurity. As advanced technology systems become increasingly prevalent across various sectors, the need for robust defence mechanisms against adversarial attacks becomes paramount. The study aims to develop and evaluate novel techniques for detecting and preventing data poisoning attacks, focusing on both theoretical frameworks and practical applications. Through a comprehensive literature review, experimental validation using the CIFAR-10 and Insurance Claims datasets, and the development of innovative algorithms, this paper seeks to enhance the resilience of AI models against malicious data manipulation. The study explores various methods, including anomaly detection, robust optimization strategies, and ensemble learning, to identify and mitigate the effects of poisoned data during model training. Experimental results indicate that data poisoning significantly degrades model performance, reducing classification accuracy by up to 27 % in image recognition tasks (CIFAR-10) and 22 % in fraud detection models (Insurance Claims dataset). The proposed defence mechanisms, including statistical anomaly detection and adversarial training, successfully mitigated poisoning effects, improving model robustness and restoring accuracy levels by an average of $15-20 \%$. The findings further demonstrate that ensemble learning techniques provide an additional layer of resilience, reducing false positives and false negatives caused by adversarial data injections. The findings of this paper contribute to the broader understanding of adversarial machine learning and provide actionable insights for practitioners in industries facing emerging threats to AI-based systems. By addressing the challenges of data poisoning attacks, this study aims to improve the security and reliability of AI models, ultimately fostering greater trust in AI technologies across critical applications.

papers.title: Robust and Adaptive Dual-Defense Framework Against Data Poisoning Attacks in Recommendation Systems
papers.abstract: Deep learning-based recommendation systems are highly vulnerable to data poisoning attacks, where adversaries manipulate user interactions to degrade model integrity. We hypothesize that combining an active robust loss with a passive GAN-based detection will significantly reduce poisoning impact in recommendation systems without sacrificing utility. We propose a robust and adaptive dual-defense framework: the active defense integrates a crafted loss function to mitigate poisoning effects while maintaining model performance. The passive defense employs a Generative Adversarial Network (GAN)-based detection model to identify and filter poisoned data, enhancing detection accuracy and system security. The framework supports classical matrix factorization (MF) model and large language model (LLM)-based pipelines and scales to large datasets. Extensive experiments across multiple real-world datasets at varying poison rates show that our method outperforms representative defenses, consistently reducing attack success without sacrificing recommendation quality. The framework also admits a federated instantiation, where robust training and GAN-based detection run on clients and only privacy-preserving summaries are aggregated. The proposed method significantly improves the robustness and adaptability of recommendation systems under data poisoning attacks.

papers.title: Towards Imperceptible and Robust Adversarial Example Attacks against Neural Networks
papers.abstract: Machine learning systems based on deep neural networks, being able to produce state-of-the-art results on various perception tasks, have gained mainstream adoption in many applications. However, they are shown to be vulnerable to adversarial example attack, which generates malicious output by adding slight perturbations to the input. Previous adversarial example crafting methods, however, use simple metrics to evaluate the distances between the original examples and the adversarial ones, which could be easily detected by human eyes. In addition, these attacks are often not robust due to the inevitable noises and deviation in the physical world. In this work, we present a new adversarial example attack crafting method, which takes the human perceptual system into consideration and maximizes the noise tolerance of the crafted adversarial example. Experimental results demonstrate the efficacy of the proposed technique.

papers.title: Robust Real-World Image Super-Resolution against Adversarial Attacks
papers.abstract: Recently deep neural networks (DNNs) have achieved significant success in real-world image super-resolution (SR). However, adversarial image samples with quasi-imperceptible noises could threaten deep learning SR models. In this paper, we propose a robust deep learning framework for real-world SR that randomly erases potential adversarial noises in the frequency domain of input images or features. The rationale is that on the SR task clean images or features have a different pattern from the attacked ones in the frequency domain. Observing that existing adversarial attacks usually add high-frequency noises to input images, we introduce a novel random frequency mask module that blocks out high-frequency components possibly containing the harmful perturbations in a stochastic manner. Since the frequency masking may not only destroys the adversarial perturbations but also affects the sharp details in a clean image, we further develop an adversarial sample classifier based on the frequency domain of images to determine if applying the proposed mask module. Based on the above ideas, we devise a novel real-world image SR framework that combines the proposed frequency mask modules and the proposed adversarial classifier with an existing super-resolution backbone network. Experiments show that our proposed method is more insensitive to adversarial attacks and presents more stable SR results than existing models and defenses.

literature_themes.theme: Data Poisoning Attacks and Defense Mechanisms in AI Models
literature_themes.summary: This cluster of papers focuses on the detection and prevention of data poisoning attacks on AI models, particularly in the contexts of image recognition and recommendation systems. The studies propose various defense mechanisms, including anomaly detection, robust optimization, and dual-defense frameworks that integrate active and passive defenses to enhance model resilience against malicious data manipulation. Experimental results demonstrate significant improvements in model performance and security against such attacks.
literature_themes.limitations: The papers highlight the effectiveness of proposed methods but may lack comprehensive evaluations across diverse datasets and real-world scenarios. Additionally, the third paper does not provide an abstract, limiting insights into its contributions and findings.
literature_themes.gap_relevance: This cluster identifies critical vulnerabilities in AI models due to data poisoning and suggests innovative defense strategies, thereby supporting research gap identification in the areas of model robustness, adversarial training, and the need for scalable defense mechanisms in various applications.

literature_themes.theme: Adversarial Robustness in Deep Learning Applications
literature_themes.summary: This cluster of papers focuses on enhancing the robustness of deep neural networks against adversarial attacks, particularly in the contexts of adversarial example generation and image super-resolution. The first paper introduces a method for crafting adversarial examples that are imperceptible to humans while maintaining robustness against real-world noise. The second paper presents a framework for image super-resolution that employs frequency domain techniques to mitigate the effects of adversarial perturbations, ensuring better performance in real-world scenarios.
literature_themes.limitations: Both studies highlight the challenges of balancing adversarial robustness with the preservation of image quality. The proposed methods may still struggle with certain types of adversarial attacks or may inadvertently affect the details of clean images. Additionally, the effectiveness of these techniques in diverse real-world conditions remains to be fully validated.
literature_themes.gap_relevance: This cluster identifies a critical research gap in developing adversarial defenses that are both effective and imperceptible, particularly in practical applications like image processing. It underscores the need for further exploration of perceptual metrics and frequency domain techniques to enhance the resilience of deep learning models against sophisticated adversarial threats.

summary: The retrieved literature addresses vulnerabilities in AI systems to data poisoning and adversarial attacks, proposing various defense mechanisms such as anomaly detection, dual-defense frameworks, and frequency domain techniques. While significant improvements in model robustness and performance are reported, limitations include a lack of comprehensive evaluations across diverse datasets and real-world applications. The studies underscore critical research gaps in developing adaptable and effective defenses, particularly in image processing and recommendation systems, highlighting the need for further exploration of scalable solutions.
scholarly_positioning: Despite significant advancements in defending AI systems against data poisoning and adversarial attacks, existing literature reveals unresolved tensions in the generalizability and adaptability of proposed defense mechanisms. While techniques such as anomaly detection and dual-defense frameworks have shown promise, they often lack comprehensive evaluations across diverse datasets and real-world scenarios, limiting their applicability. Furthermore, the focus on specific applications, such as recommendation systems and image processing, highlights a critical gap in developing scalable and robust defenses that can be generalized across various AI domains. This proposed research aims to address these limitations by exploring innovative, adaptable defense strategies that enhance the resilience of AI systems against sophisticated threats, thereby contributing to the broader discourse on AI security and robustness.
research_scope: This empirical study will evaluate the effectiveness of a dual-defense framework combining anomaly detection and frequency domain techniques against data poisoning and adversarial attacks in image recognition systems. The target population will consist of deep neural network models trained on diverse datasets, including CIFAR-10 and ImageNet, over a six-month evaluation period. The study will compare the performance of the proposed defense framework against a baseline model without these defenses. Primary outcomes will include classification accuracy and robustness metrics against both data poisoning and adversarial examples, while secondary outcomes will assess the impact on image quality and processing time. This research aims to provide comprehensive insights into the adaptability and generalizability of defense mechanisms across varying AI applications.
concept_definition:
{
  "Robust AI Systems": "AI systems designed to maintain performance and reliability despite malicious attempts to manipulate data or model behavior.",
  "Data Poisoning": "A type of attack where an adversary injects misleading data into the training set to degrade the model's performance.",
  "Adversarial Attacks": "Techniques that involve creating inputs specifically designed to mislead AI models, often by exploiting model vulnerabilities.",
  "Dual-Defense Framework": "A combined approach that utilizes two distinct defense mechanisms—anomaly detection and frequency domain techniques—to enhance system robustness.",
  "Anomaly Detection": "A method for identifying unusual patterns in data that do not conform to expected behavior, used to flag potentially malicious inputs.",
  "Frequency Domain Techniques": "Approaches that analyze data in the frequency domain (e.g., using Fourier transforms) to detect and mitigate adversarial perturbations.",
  "Image Recognition Systems": "AI models, particularly deep neural networks, that are trained to identify and classify objects within images.",
  "Classification Accuracy": "The percentage of correct predictions made by the model compared to the total number of predictions.",
  "Robustness Metrics": "Quantitative measures that evaluate how well a model performs under adversarial conditions or when subjected to data poisoning.",
  "Image Quality": "The fidelity and clarity of images processed by the model, which may be affected by defense mechanisms.",
  "Processing Time": "The duration taken by the model to process inputs and produce outputs, which can be impacted by the complexity of defense mechanisms.",
  "Generalizability": "The ability of a defense mechanism to perform effectively across different datasets and applications beyond the specific conditions under which it was tested.",
  "Trust Calibration": "The alignment between a user's confidence in the AI system's predictions and the actual accuracy of those predictions, ensuring users can rely on the system appropriately."
}
technical_feasibility: The proposed study requires access to labeled datasets such as CIFAR-10 and ImageNet, as well as GPU resources for training deep neural networks. It does not require human participants or ethics approval since it focuses on model evaluation rather than user interaction. The study does not necessitate open-source model access or hidden state extraction, as it evaluates performance metrics at the output level. A feasible adjustment would be to ensure that the selected models are compatible with the evaluation framework and that sufficient computational resources are allocated for the six-month evaluation period.
gap: Prior studies have demonstrated the effectiveness of dual-defense frameworks against data poisoning attacks in recommendation systems; however, they treat the adaptability of these frameworks to diverse AI applications as unresolved, leaving unclear whether their performance can be generalized to image recognition tasks. This matters practically because the vulnerabilities of AI systems extend beyond specific domains, necessitating scalable solutions. Therefore, this study investigates the effectiveness of a dual-defense framework combining anomaly detection and frequency domain techniques against data poisoning and adversarial attacks in image recognition systems.
question: How effective is a dual-defense framework combining anomaly detection and frequency domain techniques in enhancing the robustness of image recognition systems against data poisoning and adversarial attacks compared to baseline models without these defenses?
theoretical_mechanism: The proposed research investigates the effectiveness of a dual-defense framework, where the independent variable is the combination of anomaly detection and frequency domain techniques. The mediator in this framework is the enhanced robustness of image recognition systems, which is expected to improve the system-level outcomes, such as classification accuracy and robustness metrics against data poisoning and adversarial attacks. The moderator may include the diversity of datasets used for training, impacting the generalizability of the defense mechanisms. The dependent variable is the performance of the image recognition systems compared to baseline models without defenses. The theoretical framework is grounded in the concept of robustness in AI systems, where the causal chain suggests that effective defense mechanisms lead to improved system performance, thereby enhancing user-level outcomes like trust and reliance on the AI system. Assumptions requiring empirical validation include the effectiveness of the dual-defense framework across diverse datasets and its scalability to various AI applications.
hypothesis: The implementation of a dual-defense framework combining anomaly detection and frequency domain techniques (independent variable) will result in significantly higher classification accuracy (primary dependent variable) and improved robustness metrics against data poisoning and adversarial attacks compared to baseline models without these defenses, indicating a positive effect of the dual-defense framework on system performance.

proposal: This research proposal aims to investigate the effectiveness of a dual-defense framework that integrates anomaly detection and frequency domain techniques to enhance the robustness of image recognition systems against data poisoning and adversarial attacks. Key concepts include 'Robust AI Systems' as those maintaining performance despite malicious data manipulation, 'Data Poisoning' as the injection of misleading data, and 'Adversarial Attacks' as inputs designed to mislead models. The study will focus on deep neural network models trained on CIFAR-10 and ImageNet datasets over a six-month evaluation period, assuming access to labeled datasets and GPU resources, with no need for human participants. Positioned within the discourse on AI security, this research addresses critical gaps in the adaptability and generalizability of defense mechanisms across various applications, particularly highlighting that existing literature has not sufficiently explored the dual-defense framework's applicability beyond recommendation systems. The central research question is: How effective is the dual-defense framework in enhancing robustness compared to baseline models? The theoretical mechanism posits that the independent variables (anomaly detection and frequency domain techniques) will mediate enhanced robustness, leading to improved classification accuracy and robustness metrics as dependent variables. The hypothesis states that the dual-defense framework will significantly outperform baseline models in classification accuracy and robustness against attacks. Operationalization will involve measuring classification accuracy and robustness metrics post-evaluation, with controls for dataset quality and model architecture. The expected contributions include a novel theoretical construct for dual-defense strategies, a systematic methodology for evaluating adaptability across datasets, and empirical findings on performance metrics. Key limitations include potential generalizability issues beyond the tested datasets and the risk of model overfitting. Failure modes will be addressed through robust anomaly detection algorithms, continuous refinement of defense techniques, and clear communication of study boundaries.
